newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police widen search in bin-bag killings.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police widen search in bin-bag killings.

text.p: Belgian police searching for clues after the weekend discovery of bin bags containing the surgically severed limbs of three women found a new bag on Monday with what media reports described as personal effects.

The nine bags containing the limbs of the three victims were found by chance in a ditch next to the Brussels-Paris railway line on Saturday by a passing mounted policeman in the town of Cuesmes, near Mons in southern Belgium.
No details were immediately available of the exact contents of the 10th bag found on Monday, or whether it might help police identify the victims.
The heads and torsos have not been found, and on Monday police widened the area of search.
Mons Public Prosecutor Pierre Honore said the severed arms and legs had been transferred to a hospital for scientific analysis. But he warned identification could take some time.
"It will be slow. At least 15 days," he told RTBF television.
Police said it was clear from the state of the ground under the bags that they had been left in the ditch at different times.
"There are three different types of putrefaction," Honore said. "One very advanced, one less so, and one quite recent."
He said Mons police had contacted forces in other areas of the country.
Five of the nine bags found at the weekend had the name of the Belgian beach resort of Knokke-Heist printed on them.
Police said they had no clue as to the identity of the killer or killers -- other than that they appeared to have some surgical knowledge of anatomy -- or to the motives.
They said the investigation into the origin of the limbs would focus on recent disappearances of women in Belgium and France.
Newspapers said two of the dead had been adult women, and the third had been either an adolescent or a young woman.
They said the surgical nature of the dismemberment had prompted speculation of links with the discovery in July last year of the mutilated corpse of another woman in the same region.
Police officials said at the weekend there was no immediate reason to suspect a link with gruesome discoveries made in a paedophile scandal which has rocked the country in the past nine months.
The bodies of five young girls have been found since August.

Convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux has been charged with the murder of four of them. Another convicted paedophile, Patrick Derochette, has been charged with the illegal imprisonment and rape of a minor leading to death.
